questions.q: An invitation asks you to "review the minutes of the previous meeting". What document does minutes refer to here?
options: The written record of the previous meeting’s proceedings and decisions.
The schedule showing the duration of each presentation at the next meeting.
The invoices recording the cost of holding the previous meeting.
The attendance timetable used only to record employees’ working hours.
questions.explanation: Meeting minutes are the record of proceedings, decisions and actions. The word does not mean a duration measurement in this expression.

questions.q: Participants supported a proposal in principle, subject to budget approval. Which wording preserves the condition?
options: The proposal was rejected because a budget review is still pending.
The proposal has support in principle, subject to budget approval.
The proposal has final approval and can be implemented without further checks.
The budget has already been approved because participants supported the idea.
questions.explanation: L’accord de principe ne remplace pas la validation budgétaire attendue. La condition doit être conservée sans présenter l’option comme rejetée ou définitivement autorisée.

questions.q: The minutes say "The chair invited members to comment on the proposal". Who does chair identify in this sentence?
options: The person who takes every operational action after the meeting, regardless of role.
The supplier presenting a quotation, regardless of who presides.
The person presiding over the meeting.
Every participant entitled to speak, treated as a single role.
questions.explanation: The chair is the person who presides. The role is distinct from all members collectively, a supplier or the owner of every resulting action.

questions.q: A committee hears a recommendation to buy equipment but postpones its vote. Which minute is justified?
options: The purchase was approved, with the postponed vote serving only to record an approval already given.
The committee completed its vote and rejected the recommended purchase.
The equipment order was authorised while the approval vote remained deferred.
The purchase was recommended; the approval decision was deferred.
questions.explanation: Le compte rendu doit distinguer recommandation, décision et exécution. Un vote reporté ne peut pas être présenté comme une autorisation acquise.

questions.q: Under "Apologies", the minutes list two members who notified the organiser that they could not attend. What does this heading record?
options: Members whose notified absence is recorded.
Members admitting errors in their presentations at the meeting.
Members who voted against every proposal discussed.
Members responsible for correcting mistakes in the draft minutes.
questions.explanation: Apologies in this meeting context records notified non-attendance. It does not mean an admission of a mistake or a vote against a proposal.

questions.q: The supplied meeting rule requires at least four voting members to be present for a decision. Three are present. A minute says "The quorum was not met". What does this mean under the rule?
options: A majority of the three attendees necessarily voted against the proposal.
The required minimum attendance for making the decision was not reached.
The proposal was approved because all three attendees could discuss it.
Four favourable votes were recorded even though only three members were present.
questions.explanation: Quorum concerns the required attendance, not the vote’s substantive outcome. The question applies the rule supplied rather than assuming a universal threshold.

questions.q: A minute says “improve reporting”, with no responsible person, output or date. Which revision makes it verifiable?
options: Maya will consider reporting whenever other tasks permit, without an identified output.
A revised reporting template should be prepared, with no person or delivery date assigned.
Maya will submit a revised reporting template by 12 May.
Maya will improve reporting, with neither a specified deliverable nor a deadline.
questions.explanation: Une action vérifiable identifie un responsable, un livrable et une échéance. Les autres formulations expriment des intentions générales plutôt qu’un engagement contrôlable.

questions.q: An action was agreed, but no deadline was set. What should the minutes state?
options: Due on the date suggested informally by one participant but not agreed.
Due on the next meeting date, even though the meeting set no such deadline.
Due on the previous project’s deadline, carried forward without confirmation.
Deadline to be confirmed
questions.explanation: Un compte rendu fidèle signale la date manquante au lieu de l’inventer. L’absence d’échéance ne prouve ni l’achèvement ni l’annulation de l’action.

questions.q: Read the minute: "The revised purchasing limit was approved by Lina after Karim’s review." Who approved the revised limit according to this sentence?
options: Lina.
Karim.
Lina and Karim jointly, because both names appear.
The sentence identifies the reviewer but does not identify the approver.
questions.explanation: In the passive construction was approved by Lina, the by-phrase names the approver. After Karim’s review assigns a separate earlier review role.

questions.q: An action log describes a task as "outstanding" and states that it has not yet been completed. Which interpretation fits this status?
options: The task was completed to an exceptionally high standard.
The task remains to be completed.
The task has been cancelled and no longer requires action.
The task was approved as complete when it was first assigned.
questions.explanation: Outstanding in an action log means unresolved or still to be done. It is not the adjective meaning excellent in this context.

questions.q: A draft action log assigns a task to a person who was only mentioned as a possible contributor. What should the writer do?
options: Assign the task to the possible contributor without confirming whether that role was agreed.
Treat the person who proposed the task as its owner without checking the assignment.
Seek confirmation of the owner instead of inventing an assignment.
Assign final ownership to every contributor mentioned, even where none accepted that responsibility.
questions.explanation: Une responsabilité ne se déduit pas d’une simple mention. Il faut confirmer l’attribution pour ne pas créer un engagement que la réunion n’a pas établi.

questions.q: The next meeting reviews an action that is still being prepared. Which status avoids claiming completion?
options: Completed, because preparation has started
Approved, because a draft exists
Cancelled, because the task is not finished yet
In progress, with the remaining deliverable identified
questions.explanation: In progress distingue le travail engagé de son achèvement. Un brouillon ou un début d’exécution ne démontre pas une remise finale ni une approbation.

questions.q: A meeting agenda ends with "Any other business". What is the function of this item?
options: To allow additional matters to be raised under the meeting’s applicable arrangements.
To review only the accounts of companies other than the organisation holding the meeting.
To record that all matters discussed earlier have been approved without a vote.
To assign every unfinished action automatically to the meeting organiser.
questions.explanation: Any other business is a heading for additional matters. It does not itself decide them or allocate all outstanding tasks.

questions.q: All six members who vote support a motion, and no member votes against or abstains. The minute records a "unanimous vote in favour". Which meaning is preserved?
options: Only a simple majority of the six voting members supported the motion.
Every member voting supported the motion.
The chair alone supported the motion while the other five opposed it.
The members discussed the motion but did not vote on it.
questions.explanation: Unanimous means agreement by all members in the stated voting group. It should not be used as a synonym for any majority or mere discussion.

questions.q: A member "abstained" in a vote, and the record separately lists votes for and against. What does abstained mean here?
options: The member cast a vote against the motion.
The member cast a vote for the motion.
The member did not cast a vote for or against the motion.
The member necessarily left the meeting before the vote, regardless of the attendance record.
questions.explanation: Abstention is distinct from a vote against and from a vote in favour. It does not alone establish absence from the meeting.

questions.q: A participant makes a firm commitment: “I will submit the report on Monday.” Which minute preserves that commitment?
options: The participant mentioned that a report might perhaps be useful.
The report has already been submitted and approved.
The participant rejected any responsibility for the report.
The participant committed to submitting the report on Monday.
questions.explanation: Le compte rendu doit conserver la force de l’engagement sans le transformer en simple possibilité ou en tâche déjà achevée.

questions.q: A minute states "Maya said that she had submitted the report before the meeting." When does the submission occur relative to the reported statement?
options: It is presented as earlier than Maya’s statement at the meeting.
It is presented as a commitment to submit the report after the meeting.
It is presented as a request that another person submit the report later.
It is presented as a submission necessarily taking place at the next meeting.
questions.explanation: Had submitted is past perfect and places the submission before the past reporting point. It is not the future-in-the-past would submit.

questions.q: An international action log uses "09/04/2026" without a date-format convention. Readers may interpret day and month differently. Which replacement removes that ambiguity if the intended date is 9 April?
options: 09/04/26, with the same unspecified day/month convention.
9 April 2026.
09-04-2026, changing only the separator without naming the month.
09.04.2026, changing only the separator without naming the month.
questions.explanation: Writing the month in words identifies April. A different separator or shorter year does not by itself settle the day/month convention.

questions.q: Two participants disagree about whether a proposal was approved. What should the minute writer do before stating final approval?
options: Record the version preferred by the chair without checking whether approval or only discussion was recorded.
Merge the two conflicting accounts into an approval statement without resolving the disputed condition.
Identify the disputed point and seek clarification.
Treat the earlier draft of the minutes as conclusive despite the identified conflict in the supporting notes.
questions.explanation: Le désaccord doit être clarifié à partir des notes et des personnes compétentes. La concision ne justifie pas d’inventer ou de renforcer une décision.

questions.q: An agreed action date is corrected after circulation. Which approach preserves an understandable record?
options: Send an unmarked replacement and leave recipients to discover which date changed.
Keep both dates circulating without identifying which is the agreed correction.
Change only the archived original without notifying the people expected to act on the new date.
Record and communicate the correction with its status clearly identified.
questions.explanation: Une correction doit rester traçable et être communiquée aux personnes concernées. Ni la modification silencieuse ni le maintien volontaire d’une erreur ne facilite le suivi.

questions.q: Minutes contain sensitive commercial information. How should the distribution list be chosen?
options: Match recipients and channel to the purpose and authorised access.
Send the full record to everyone who attended part of the meeting without checking their access to the sensitive annexes.
Use the previous meeting’s recipient list unchanged even if the new record contains additional restricted information.
Treat receipt of the invitation alone as authorisation to receive every confidential appendix.
questions.explanation: Le contenu et les destinataires doivent correspondre au besoin et aux accès autorisés. La nature de compte rendu ne rend pas toutes les informations librement diffusables.

questions.q: A record includes an employee’s unrelated personal details that do not explain any decision. What is the most appropriate editorial check?
options: Retain the unrelated details solely because a participant mentioned them during the meeting.
Remove unnecessary details while retaining information needed for the meeting’s purpose.
Move the unnecessary details to an appendix while distributing that appendix to the same full recipient list.
Treat the details as necessary merely because they make the account more comprehensive.
questions.explanation: Un compte rendu conserve les informations utiles à son objectif. Une mention informelle n’impose pas de diffuser des détails personnels sans lien avec la décision.

questions.q: A polished draft contradicts the supporting notes about who approves a purchase. Which quality should take priority?
options: Retain the polished attribution until a later meeting, despite the known contradiction about approval authority.
Use the draft’s fluent wording as a substitute for checking the decision recorded in the notes.
Accuracy of the decision and approval role
Keep the draft and supporting notes inconsistent while treating both as the final authoritative record.
questions.explanation: La qualité d’un compte rendu repose d’abord sur l’exactitude des décisions et responsabilités. Une présentation soignée ne rend pas correcte une attribution erronée.
